pairs.subject: copy-quality-gates
pairs.evidence: docs/i18n/copy-contract.json:14 The copy gate's only landing source is a one-segment glob. It matches app/_landing/parts.tsx but not app/_landing/cosmos/Cosmos.tsx or any cosmos/engine/*.ts module. A run I did (read-only) printed 'checked 22 strings ... in 31 files' and OK, while docs/i18n/style-en.md:37-38 still says the landing is gated: a green run over a coverage hole.

techniques.evidence: docs/i18n/copy-contract.json:14 The extractor reads aria-label (PROSE_ATTRS), but the glob leaves out Cosmos.tsx ('Back', 'Path', 'Search', 'Depth', 'Results'). The report neither extracts the engine's code literals nor declares them out of scope, so the hole has a green light over it.

app/_landing/cosmos/engine/nav.ts:161 This accessible name is built by concatenating fragments in code, which is an L1 deterministic class. Similar concatenations sit at stage.ts:94 and library.ts:92. No check sees them, because the engine .ts files are outside every gated source.

docs/i18n/copy-contract.json:11 A contract declares variant, dash, case and terms, and its _notes record counts against the real strings. style-en.md:18 records the wordless-landing brief as a house ruling. No exemplars or fact sheet, which matters little for a wordless page.
docs/i18n/copy-contract.json:26 Off/warn/error per rule is contract data, not code. style-en.md:51 requires the reason for any override to be recorded beside it.
app/_landing/parts.tsx:89 The landing copy is hardcoded English JSX with no target locales. With fewer than two checked locales there is no agreement to read.

pairs.registryProposal: rendered-string-extraction could name a 'source moved under its glob' incident shape. A gated surface was refactored into a subdirectory, the one-segment glob kept matching the one file left behind, the string count still printed, and the scope document kept claiming coverage. The fix would be a fixture or check that each declared-gated surface still contributes at least N strings.
